committed: Before any implementation output was inspected: this file and the validation contract in DETECTION.md were committed ahead of js/measure/detect.js, the validation tool and the oracle's fixtures. A check that a measurement crosses is a failed check, not a reason to move the bound; only Carl resets a threshold, with a register row.

background.level: the clipped median of each box
background.noise: the clipped standard deviation of each box
background.interpolation: bilinear between box centres, constant beyond the first and last centre
background.masked: masked, non-finite and saturated pixels are left out of every box

smoothing.kernel: Gaussian of the stated FWHM, truncated at 3 sigma (radius ceil(3 sigma)), summing to 1
smoothing.edges: the nearest edge pixel is repeated (astropy boundary 'extend'); a masked pixel is left out and the kernel renormalised over the pixels that remain
smoothing.noiseScale: the smoothed noise of a pixel is its local noise times the square root of the kernel's sum of squares

detection.rule: a pixel is above threshold when the smoothed, background-subtracted value is greater than sigma times its smoothed noise; segments are the 8-connected runs of such pixels with at least minArea pixels; deblending is off

properties.position: first moment of the unsmoothed background-subtracted values in the segment, negative values set to zero (photutils SourceCatalog)
properties.shape: second central moments of the same weights, +1/12 on the diagonal while the determinant is under 1/144 (SourceExtractor's rule, as photutils); semimajor and semiminor sigma, ellipticity 1 - b/a, orientation counter-clockwise from +x in degrees
properties.flux: the aperture of Prompt 180 (r = 1.5 FWHM, annulus 3 to 5 FWHM, exact edges) at the segment position, no recentring

flags.saturated: a pixel of the segment at or above the contract's saturation or linearity limit
flags.edge: the segment touches the frame's border
flags.masked: a masked pixel is adjacent to the segment (8-neighbourhood)
flags.crowded: another source is nearer than the outer annulus radius plus the aperture radius (Prompt 180's rule)
flags.sharp: the brightest pixel holds more than half of the segment's flux

psf.gaussian: pixel-integrated circular Gaussian (erf over each pixel), parameters flux, x, y, FWHM
psf.moffat: circular Moffat, FWHM = 2 alpha sqrt(2^(1/beta) - 1), integrated over each pixel by 5 by 5 sub-pixel midpoints, parameters flux, x, y, FWHM, beta
psf.fit: Levenberg-Marquardt on the background-subtracted pixels of a square of half width ceil(2.5 max(FWHM0, 2.5)); weights 1 / (local noise squared + model counts) refreshed at each step, or none
psf.selection: unflagged, signal to noise (Prompt 180) at least 30, ellipticity at most 0.3, at most 25 stars, brightest first
psf.combination: inverse-variance mean of the FWHMs, its sigma times the square root of reduced chi-square when that exceeds 1
psf.profile: the stacked radial profile: each star's pixels binned by distance from its fitted position in bins of 0.5 pixel, normalised by its fitted flux, averaged over stars, with the standard error of the mean

grid.what: twelve stars per frame, one per cell of a 4 by 3 grid; x in [32 i + 12, 32 i + 20], y in [42 j + 12, 42 j + 30], uniform, so no star is within 24 pixels of another or within 12 of an edge

a1.falsePositives.what: detections not within 2 pixels of an injected star, per frame, on 300 frames of sky and noise only, on frames carrying twelve stars at each depth (150 each), and (d1) on 150 frames with a strong linear gradient and no stars

gradient.what: an added plane of 1.0 ADU per pixel along x and 0.7 along y, which is 192 and 134 electrons across the frame (15 and 11 times the sky noise)

a1.recovery.what: fraction of injected stars with a detection within 2 pixels, per depth

a1.position.what: root mean square distance between the detected position and the injected position, per depth, pixels

a1.flux.what: mean and root mean square of z = (net - F * EE(r)) / sigma_stated for the flux the list reports, per depth; EE is the analytic encircled energy of the Gaussian at the aperture radius 1.5 FWHM

a2.shape.what: elliptical Gaussian stars, flux 30000 electrons, sigma 2.2 and 1.2 pixels (ellipticity 0.4545), orientations -75, -30, 15, 45 and 80 degrees, 40 frames of twelve (480 stars): mean error of the ellipticity, mean absolute error of the orientation; and circular stars of the same flux: the fraction with ellipticity at most 0.06

a3.psfGaussian.what: the Gaussian fit to stars of 20000 electrons on the detector kernel's own point-spread function of FWHM 2.0, 3.0 and 4.5 pixels, 25 frames of twelve (300 stars) each, positions from the detections: relative bias of the mean FWHM, and the largest relative error of a frame's combined FWHM

a3.psfMoffat.what: the Moffat fit (beta free) to Moffat stars of FWHM 3 and beta 2.5, 20000 electrons, drawn on 15 by 15 sub-pixels, 25 frames of twelve: relative bias of the mean FWHM

a4.profile.what: the stacked radial profile of the stars of a3.psfGaussian at FWHM 3 against the same bins of the noiseless truth image: |z| of every one of the first ten bins at most 4; and the half-maximum width read from the stack against the truth image's, relative

b1.mesh.what: the background and noise meshes (clipped median and clipped standard deviation of each 16 pixel box) against photutils Background2D on the same frames, and the interpolated maps against scipy's bilinear interpolation of that mesh, relative

b2.segmentation.what: the smoothed image against astropy.convolution.convolve, the number of sources and every segment's pixel count against photutils detect_sources (connectivity 8) with the same threshold map and the same mask, and each source's area, first moments, second moments, ellipticity, orientation, peak and segment flux against photutils SourceCatalog, on the pinned frames; counts and areas exact, the rest relative

b3.fwhmGaussian.what: the unweighted Gaussian fit with the background held at zero against photutils.psf.fit_fwhm (CircularGaussianPRF, the same square of pixels), relative FWHM

b4.fwhmMoffat.what: the unweighted Moffat fit against scipy least_squares with photutils.psf.MoffatPSF averaged over the same 5 by 5 sub-pixels, converged to the tolerance of the arithmetic: relative FWHM and relative beta

c1.coverage68.what: fraction of the ensemble with |FWHM fit - truth| <= 1 stated sigma, Gaussian fit with the weights, one star each, 800 stars per level (frames of twelve), levels 1500, 6000 and 40000 electrons

c2.combinedCoverage.what: the FWHM combined over the selected stars of a frame against the truth, 250 frames of twelve stars of 6000 electrons: the fraction within 1 and within 1.96 stated sigma

d2.saturated.what: a star of 600000 electrons on a detector whose pixels clip at 50000 electrons is flagged 'saturated' in the list, is left out of the selection, and a fit asked for at its position is refused with the code 'saturated' and returns no FWHM

d3.sharp.what: single-pixel events of 8000 electrons on an unmasked pixel (a cosmic ray or a hot pixel) are flagged 'sharp'; stars of 6000 electrons at FWHM 3 and 2 are not

d4.masks.what: with masked pixels in the frame: no segment contains a masked pixel (every frame); a star with three pixels masked beside its core is flagged 'masked' (fraction); a masked pixel of 100000 electrons produces no source (fraction)

d5.contract.what: display-only, no sidecar, light in unknown units, an incomplete contract, a raw frame, a lossy history: each refused with its own code and no source list

d6.edge.what: a star whose centre is 3 pixels from the border is flagged 'edge'; and a PSF fit asked for within the half width of the border is refused with 'edge' and no number

d7.noDeblending.what: two stars of 6000 electrons 5 pixels apart come out as one source (50 of 50 frames) that the PSF selection leaves out (at least 0.95); two stars 14 pixels apart come out as two sources both flagged 'crowded' (50 of 50)

d8.modelLimited.what: the Gaussian fit to Moffat stars of beta 2 and 20000 electrons is labelled model-limited (at least 0.95 of 100 stars) and the Gaussian fit to Gaussian stars of 6000 electrons is not (at most 0.02 of 800)

e2.authentic.what: one authentic frame from Prompt 189 under a fixed analysis contract: the source list and the FWHM against photutils on the same pixels
e2.authentic.status: NOT RUN until Prompt 189 lands an authentic image pack; nothing was downloaded or fabricated for this leg
